exposure: prenatal exposure to particulate matter with aerodynamic diameter <=2.5 mm (PM2.5)
outcome: child growth trajectories (slow growth, normal growth, rapid growth)
cohort: The study enrolled 6407 mother-infant pairs followed from 2015 to 2021.
finding: Prenatal exposure to PM2.5 and its components, particularly between 10-22 weeks of gestation, was associated with a higher risk of rapid growth in boys and a higher risk of slow growth in girls.
